name: perf
description: Network performance on an emulated path (pathlab: delay, rate, queue, loss in userspace): RTT and the curl timing breakdown, slow start vs a reused connection, window-limited throughput vs the BDP, bufferbloat with deep vs short queues, UDP overload, TCP throughput under loss vs the Mathis model (CUBIC vs BBR), goodput vs throughput from a sender capture, and a PMTUD black hole with PLPMTUD recovery and MSS clamping

nodes.name: router
setup: ip tuntap add dev pl-ab mode tun && ip tuntap add dev pl-ba mode tun && ip link set pl-ab up && ip link set pl-ba up && sysctl -qw net.ipv4.conf.pl-ab.rp_filter=0 net.ipv4.conf.pl-ba.rp_filter=0 && ip rule add iif eth0 table 100 && ip route add default dev pl-ab table 100 && ip rule add iif eth1 table 101 && ip route add default dev pl-ba table 101

checks.name: the emulated path: 25 ms each way, nothing else yet
ping: the RTT is the two 25 ms delays plus a fraction of a millisecond
curl's timing breakdown for a small HTTPS API call (server adds 100 ms of work): TCP 1 RTT, TLS 1.3 1 RTT, request 1 RTT + 100 ms
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; curl -s -o /dev/null --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/api-ca.pem -w 'dns %{time_namelookup}  tcp %{time_connect}  tls %{time_appconnect}  first byte %{time_starttransfer}  total %{time_total}  (%{size_download} bytes)\n' https://api.perf.test:8443/

checks.name: 4 MiB twice in one curl run: the second transfer reuses the connection — no handshakes, and slow start is already done
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; curl -s -o /dev/null -o /dev/null --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/files-ca.pem -w 'dns %{time_namelookup}  tcp %{time_connect}  tls %{time_appconnect}  first byte %{time_starttransfer}  total %{time_total}  (%{size_download} bytes)\n' https://files.perf.test:9443/ https://files.perf.test:9443/

checks.name: add a 20 Mbit/s bottleneck with a 100-packet queue: BDP = 20 Mbit/s × 50 ms = 125 KB
throughput is capped at window ÷ RTT: 16 KB → ~2.6 Mbit/s, 64 KB → ~10.5 Mbit/s, autotuned → the link
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -t 5 -w 16K -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); e=j["end"]; print("%s: %.2f Mbit/s received, %s retransmissions" % (sys.argv[1], e["sum_received"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6, e["sum_sent"].get("retransmits")))' "window 16K"; iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -t 5 -w 64K -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); e=j["end"]; print("%s: %.2f Mbit/s received, %s retransmissions" % (sys.argv[1], e["sum_received"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6, e["sum_sent"].get("retransmits")))' "window 64K"; iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -t 5  -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); e=j["end"]; print("%s: %.2f Mbit/s received, %s retransmissions" % (sys.argv[1], e["sum_received"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6, e["sum_sent"].get("retransmits")))' "window auto";

checks.name: a deep bottleneck queue: 1000 packets = 600 ms at 20 Mbit/s
CUBIC fills it: full throughput, and ping (sharing the queue) waits hundreds of milliseconds
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; ping -i 0.2 -c 35 -q 198.18.101.10 > ${EVIDENCE}/ping-1000.txt & iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -t 8 -C cubic -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); e=j["end"]; print("%s: %.2f Mbit/s received, %s retransmissions" % (sys.argv[1], e["sum_received"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6, e["sum_sent"].get("retransmits")))' "queue 1000 packets"; wait; tail -1 ${EVIDENCE}/ping-1000.txt

checks.name: the same bottleneck with a 30-packet queue
nearly the same throughput, a fraction of the delay — at the price of some drops CUBIC recovers from
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; ping -i 0.2 -c 35 -q 198.18.101.10 > ${EVIDENCE}/ping-30.txt & iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -t 8 -C cubic -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); e=j["end"]; print("%s: %.2f Mbit/s received, %s retransmissions" % (sys.argv[1], e["sum_received"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6, e["sum_sent"].get("retransmits")))' "queue 30 packets"; wait; tail -1 ${EVIDENCE}/ping-30.txt

checks.name: UDP has no congestion control: offer 30 Mbit/s to a 20 Mbit/s bottleneck and a third is lost
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -u -b 30M -t 5 -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; s=json.load(sys.stdin)["end"]["sum"]; print("udp: sent %d datagrams, lost %d = %.1f%%, received %.1f Mbit/s" % (s["packets"], s["lost_packets"], s["lost_percent"], s["bits_per_second"]*(1-s["lost_percent"]/100)/1e6))'

checks.name: the bottleneck's own counters: drops because the queue was full
remove the bottleneck; keep the 50 ms RTT
random loss vs single-flow throughput: CUBIC near the Mathis bound (MSS/RTT × 1.22/√p), BBR barely affected
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; for p in 0.001 0.01 0.02; do ${BIN}/pathlab set -c 198.18.100.1:9911 loss=$p >/dev/null; m=$(python3 -c "print('%.1f' % (1448*8/0.0514*1.22/$p**0.5/1e6))"); for cc in cubic bbr; do iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -t 6 -C $cc -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); e=j["end"]; print("%s: %.2f Mbit/s received, %s retransmissions" % (sys.argv[1], e["sum_received"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6, e["sum_sent"].get("retransmits")))' "loss $p $cc"; done; echo "  Mathis bound at $p: $m Mbit/s"; done

checks.name: the sweep left 2% loss; set 1% for the capture
a 4 MiB HTTP download through 1% loss, captured at the SENDER (a receiver-side capture never sees the copies that were lost)

run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'curl: %{size_download} bytes in %{time_total} s\n' http://files.perf.test:8080/

checks.name: goodput vs throughput from the capture: bytes the application got vs bytes the sender put on the wire
run: tshark -r ${EVIDENCE}/goodput.pcap -Y 'ip.src==198.18.101.10' -T fields -e frame.time_relative -e ip.len -e tcp.len -e tcp.analysis.retransmission 2>/dev/null | awk '{t=$1; ip+=$2; pay+=$3; if ($4!="") {r++; rb+=$3}} END {printf "duration %.3f s; IP bytes sent %d; TCP payload sent %d, of which retransmitted %d bytes in %d segments\nthroughput (IP bytes / time) %.1f Mbit/s; goodput (4194304 file bytes / time) %.1f Mbit/s\n", t, ip, pay, rb, r, ip*8/t/1e6, 4194304*8/t/1e6}'

checks.name: no loss again; make the router's client-side link MTU 1400 — a narrow hop in the middle of the path
run: ${BIN}/pathlab set loss=0 && ip link set eth0 mtu 1400 && ip link show eth0 | grep -o 'mtu [0-9]*'

checks.name: ping with DF from the server finds it: the router answers Frag needed (mtu = 1400); tracepath reports pmtu 1400
run: ping -c1 -M do -s 1472 198.18.100.10 2>&1 | grep -iE 'frag|mtu'; ping -c1 -M do -s 1372 198.18.100.10 | grep 'bytes from'; tracepath -n 198.18.100.10 | tail -1

checks.name: break PMTUD: the router no longer sends 'fragmentation needed'
forget the learned path MTU, and turn PLPMTUD off (tcp_mtu_probing=0)
run: ip route flush cache; sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=0

checks.name: a download from the server: the handshake works, every full-size segment vanishes — a black hole
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; timeout 20 iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -R -t 10 -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sys.argv[1], "per-second Mbit/s:", " ".join("%.1f" % (i["sum"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6) for i in j["intervals"]))' "mtu_probing=0"

checks.name: PLPMTUD on (tcp_mtu_probing=1): after repeated timeouts TCP tries smaller segments itself
run: ip route flush cache; sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1

checks.name: the same download now recovers after a few seconds — slowly, from slow start
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; timeout 20 iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -R -t 10 -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sys.argv[1], "per-second Mbit/s:", " ".join("%.1f" % (i["sum"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6) for i in j["intervals"]))' "mtu_probing=1"

checks.name: PLPMTUD off again, to test the network-side fix
run: ip route flush cache; sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=0

checks.name: MSS clamping at the router: --clamp-mss-to-pmtu also considers the MTU back towards the SYN's sender
with clamping, full speed from the first second, ICMP still blocked
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy; timeout 20 iperf3 -c 198.18.101.10 -R -t 5 -J | python3 -c 'import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sys.argv[1], "per-second Mbit/s:", " ".join("%.1f" % (i["sum"]["bits_per_second"]/1e6) for i in j["intervals"]))' "clamped"
